sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in Waco, TX?
sections.html:
A Waco owner can hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or take a cash offer for the house as it is. The best fit turns on your deadline, the condition of the property and whether anything clouds the title.

Nearly half of the city's housing is renter-occupied, which means many Waco houses are held as rentals, which can matter when your house has a tenant or needs work.

  • Agent listing: more exposure, with the usual showings, inspection requests and lender timelines.
  • Do it yourself: lower cost on paper, with every disclosure and contract term in your hands.
  • Cash purchase: fewer moving parts and a flexible closing date, in exchange for a price that accounts for repairs.

sections.h2: Where is Waco and how did the city develop?
sections.html:
Waco sits in central McLennan County near where the Brazos and Bosque rivers meet, roughly seventy miles south of Dallas, and the Handbook of Texas lists Interstate 35, U.S. highways 84 and 77 and State Highway 6 among its main roads. The county seat grew from a townsite laid out on March 1, 1849, on the old Waco village ground.

Cotton drove early growth. A suspension bridge over the Brazos opened in 1870, railroads followed in the 1870s and 1880s, and by the 1890s Waco was one of the most important cotton markets in the South. Baylor University moved to Waco in 1887 after merging with Waco University, and Paul Quinn College opened there in 1872.

The city also carries a hard memory. A tornado on May 11, 1953 killed 114 people and destroyed 196 business buildings, and many shoppers moved to suburban centers afterward. Connally Air Force Base closed in 1966, and an urban renewal program that started in 1958 later steered more than $125 million into the urban core by 1978. That history explains the mix of old central neighborhoods and newer outer areas you see in listings today.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Waco housing?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Waco at $221,700 for 2020-2024, and only 49.4 percent of units are owner-occupied. That ratio is lower than in many Texas cities, which shapes who is likely to buy.

sections.h2: How big is Waco and what does that mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Waco covers 88.73 square miles of land with about 1,561 residents per square mile in 2020, so it is a spread-out city with distinct areas rather than one dense core. Mean travel to work is 18.7 minutes, and a short commute is a selling point worth mentioning in a listing.

Census data also show the economy in numbers: retail sales were about $3.44 billion in 2022, health care and social assistance receipts reached roughly $2.04 billion, and accommodation and food services sales were about $676 million. Hospitals, universities and shops all support steady demand for housing near them.

Median gross rent of $1,165 gives landlords and investors a rough yardstick when they price an offer for a rental house. If you are selling a house with a lease, tell buyers about the lease term early, because it affects who can occupy the house after closing.

sections.h2: How do McLennan County tax dates affect a Waco sale?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so what you owe on a Waco house comes from local units that set their own rates after the appraisal district values the property as of January 1. Ask the McLennan County tax office for the current bill and any past-due balance before you sign a contract.

  • Notices of appraised value for homesteads go out around April 1, and others around May 1.
  • Most protests are due by May 15 or the thirtieth day after the notice is delivered, whichever is later.
  • Tax bills are mailed around October 1, with half due by November 30 for owners who split payments and the rest by June 30.
  • Unpaid tax turns delinquent on February 1.

The school district homestead exemption is $140,000 under state law, and owners 65 or older or disabled get a further $60,000 from school districts. A disabled veteran may qualify for an exemption of up to $12,000 depending on the disability rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent disabled can receive a total exemption on the homestead. The homestead appraisal cap limits yearly increases in appraised value to 10 percent.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Waco house sale?
sections.html:
The deed is filed with the county clerk of the county where the land sits, which for Waco is McLennan County. To be recorded, the instrument must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or another officer allowed to take acknowledgments, or sworn before two subscribing witnesses.

The clerk manual lists a recording charge of $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with $0.25 for each name past five that must be indexed. Separate clerk fees for records management, archive and technology can apply on top of that. A missing mailing address for the grantee may add $25. Ask the McLennan County Clerk for the total on your particular deed before closing.

Special deed types matter in Waco estates and tax sales. A sheriff's deed, trustee's deed, tax deed and general or special warranty deed all go into the same deed records, and a quitclaim deed is recorded the same way. Your title company will tell you which form your sale needs.

sections.h2: What should a Waco seller know about liens, inheritance and tenants?
sections.html:
Taxes are secured by a lien that attaches each January 1, so unpaid years follow the house to a new owner and must be paid at or before closing. A seller with delinquent taxes can ask about an installment plan, which some collectors allow for up to 36 months on a homestead.

For an inherited Waco house, an affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the county clerk, but no law forces a title company or buyer to accept it. A small estate affidavit is available only when the estate is $75,000 or less, excluding the homestead, and a court must approve it. If a tenant refuses to leave, a justice court case follows a written notice, and a writ of possession cannot issue until six days after judgment.

When foreclosure is looming, the servicer must mail the notice of sale at least 21 days ahead, and the sale takes place on a first Tuesday. Selling before that date can protect your equity, so check with your lender about payoff figures right away.

faqs.q: Is Waco a good place to sell a rental house?
faqs.a: It can be. About half of Waco's occupied homes are rentals, and the median gross rent is $1,165, so investors are active buyers. A house with a lease in place should be described with the lease terms attached.

faqs.q: How is tax split when I sell my Waco house?
faqs.a: Tax for the year is normally prorated at closing between seller and buyer. The January 1 lien covers the whole year, so any unpaid earlier years must be paid out of the proceeds or before the sale.

faqs.q: Can a house with a lien or back taxes be sold in Waco?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff comes out of the sale price, and a title company will show the amounts. Ask the tax office for a payoff letter, since penalty and interest keep growing each month on unpaid tax.

faqs.q: What if my Waco house is in an estate?
faqs.a: Ownership has to be documented first. Depending on the case, that means probate, a muniment of title or a recorded transfer on death deed, and a will generally must be probated within four years of death.

faqs.q: Do cash buyers close faster than agents in Waco?
faqs.a: Often, because there is no mortgage underwriting. The actual timeline still depends on title work, so clear liens and gather probate papers early.
